title: Share a Long Text Thread as One Image on iPhone
description: Stitch a long iPhone text conversation into one image. Keep the messages in order, remove private details and check the saved image before sending.
direct: Choose the needed messages, preserve their order, and stitch successive screenshots into one image you can read at normal zoom.
figureAlt: Overhead desk with three narrow paper strips of abstract chat balloons, without text, arranged with one strip slightly overlapping the next
cards.decision.heading: Choose where the story starts
cards.decision.body: Start with the first message that gives enough context. Stop after the exchange the recipient needs. If the thread changes subjects, two short images can be easier to read than one long image.
sections.detail-1.heading: Check the image after sending
sections.detail-1.body: Some chat apps compress long images. If the recipient cannot read individual messages at a useful zoom, share smaller sections or send the stitched image as a file where that option is available.
sections.detail-2.heading: About the app
sections.detail-2.body: Space Sheep Studio develops this iPhone app. Check the App Store listing for current access and export options.
faqs.first-question.heading: Can I take a full-page screenshot?
faqs.first-question.body: Some iPhone views support full-page capture. Use separate screenshots if the conversation view offers no full-page option.
faqs.second-question.heading: Does the image preserve every message?
faqs.second-question.body: It shows what you captured. Keep the thread if you need the full record.

steps.step-1.text: Take screenshots from top to bottom. Include one message of overlap before cropping.
steps.step-2.text: Crop private notifications, contact details and unrelated replies before you import.
steps.step-3.text: Stitch the screenshots vertically in Combine Photos: Stitch & Grid. Inspect the seams and open the saved image in Photos or Files.
